stories.title: Stockbridge Buys Maryland Industrial Property for $57M
stories.excerpt: Stockbridge has acquired a 203,000-square-foot industrial property in Maryland for $56.6 million, almost four years after seller TA Realty bought the facility for about the same price. The San Francisco-based investment management firm purchased the Class A building at 8511 Pepco Place in Upper Marlboro, Md., according to Cushman & Wakefield, which represented the seller. CoStar first reported the news. The 13-acre property is fully leased to Harris Company, a mechanical contractor that has become a major service provider to hyperscale data center operators. Harris first occupied about 34 percent of the building before recently expanding to fill the entire space. The facility was built in 2008 about half a mile east of the Capital Beltway and near Joint Base Andrews. It includes a 190-foot truck court, 26 dock doors, two drive-in doors, 218 parking spaces and roughly 75 trailer spots. TA Realty acquired the asset from an affiliate of electrical distributor Sonepar in 2022 for $56.2 million. Harris’ expansion comes as Greater Washington’s data center industry drives demand for industrial space tied to construction, infrastructure and operations. Cushman & Wakefield’s Jonathan Carpenter, Graham Savage, Dawes Milchling and James Check worked on the transaction. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Stockbridge acquired 203k-sf industrial property in Upper Marlboro, MD for $56.6M
Harris Company expanded from 34% to 100% occupancy; serves hyperscale data center operators
Property fully leased, near Capital Beltway and Joint Base Andrews with robust logistics infrastructure
stories.summary: Stockbridge paid $56.6 million for a fully-leased Class A industrial building in Upper Marlboro, Maryland, nearly matching the $56.2 million TA Realty paid in 2022. The tenant, Harris Company, has expanded to occupy the entire 203,000-square-foot facility after initially leasing only 34%, driven by strong demand as a major service provider to hyperscale data center operators. The asset's location near the Capital Beltway and Joint Base Andrews, combined with robust dock and trailer infrastructure, reflects its value for logistics and tech-adjacent operations.
stories.impact: The full-occupancy expansion by a hyperscale data center services provider signals sustained demand in the Washington DC metro region for industrial and logistics real estate. While not direct multifamily impact, this reinforces job and capital inflow to Northern Virginia and the broader DC corridor, supporting residential demand and rental growth in adjacent submarkets (Arlington, Alexandria, Bethesda) where tech and defense contractor employees concentrate.

stories.title: Inside Ken Griffin’s $3B Bet on Miami’s Wynwood
stories.excerpt: Three years ago, staffers working for billionaire financier Ken Griffin met with Moishe Mana to present him the deal of lifetime: They offered about $800 million for his 35-acre portfolio in Miami’s Wynwood neighborhood. Surprised, Mana initially rejected the offer. His properties were not for sale, and he envisioned developing his own business and entertainment district. But three days later, the investor relented. “Once I understood that this is going to be good for Miami,” Mana explained at a press event Thursday. “It’s completing our vision, not competing. I said, ‘Let’s go.’” The cash deal, which ultimately ballooned to $1.1 billion, closed this week without any outside debt and partners for Griffin. It marked one of the largest commercial real estate transactions in the country’s history. What’s more: Griffin pledged an additional $2 billion to Carnegie Mellon University, bringing his total giving to $3 billion — the largest combined donation to higher education from a private individual. $1 billion of the gift will support the university’s Pittsburgh campus, while $2 billion will support the launch of CMU Miami and includes the value of the real estate. The gift will help address one of Miami’s biggest challenges as it seeks to become a global business hub: its lack of top-tier universities, which are crucial to create a pipeline of employable grads for tech and finance companies. “If you look at Pittsburgh and the economic renaissance taking place: 250 tech startups, 100 companies focused on robotics,” Griffin said during a public address Thursday. “The future of America is being built in Pittsburgh — that future will be strengthened by what we build in Miami.” The Wynwood campus is expected to house more than 3,500 undergraduates, master’s, and PhD students as well as nearly 300 faculty members, and more than 600 staff. bullets: Ken Griffin paid $1.1B for Moishe Mana's 35-acre Wynwood portfolio in Miami
Griffin pledged additional $2B to Carnegie Mellon, signaling $3B total philanthropic commitment to Miami region
All-cash deal closed without external debt or partners; largest CRE transaction in recent U.S. history
stories.summary: Ken Griffin's Citadel closed a $1.1 billion all-cash acquisition of Moishe Mana's 35-acre Wynwood portfolio in Miami this week, representing one of the largest commercial real estate transactions in U.S. history. Griffin simultaneously pledged $2 billion to Carnegie Mellon University, bringing his total giving to $3 billion. The cash deal, completed without external financing or partners, signals Griffin's substantial capital deployment and long-term conviction in Miami's economic and real estate fundamentals.
stories.impact: A $3B capital commitment by a billionaire financier to Miami—including real estate ownership and university investment—dramatically accelerates expectations for talent inflow, job creation, and demand for residential housing across Miami-Dade. Wynwood's transformation into a mixed-use destination anchored by Griffin capital and Carnegie Mellon's expanded presence (likely research, tech, and professional services jobs) will drive renter migration and rent growth in adjacent urban neighborhoods and central Miami submarkets within 2–5 years. This also signals confidence in Miami's investment climate and may lower cap rates city-wide, improving development economics for multifamily.

stories.title: JLL Closes Sale of Grocery-Anchored Somerset County Center
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets closed the sale of The Hills Village Center, a 110,000-square-foot grocery-anchored retail property located at 550 Hills Dr. in Bedminster, NJ. Senior managing directors Jose Cruz and Kevin O’Hearn, senior director J.B. Bruno and senior associate Cole Doyon. represented the seller, Lena Centers, a Longpoint Partners subsidiary. Asana Partners acquired the asset. The price was not disclosed. Fully leased, The Hills Village Center is anchored by Kings Food Markets and CVS and features a diverse tenant mix including Starbucks, PNC Bank, Peapack Gladstone Bank and multiple dining establishments and service-oriented retailers. “Lena Centers has cultivated a thriving retail destination that serves as the commercial hub for The Hills community and surrounding areas,” said Cruz. “The successful disposition to Asana Partners reflects both the quality of the asset and the strength of the Somerset County retail market, where strong demographics and limited competition continue to drive investor interest.” The post JLL Closes Sale of Grocery-Anchored Somerset County Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL closed sale of 110k-sf Hills Village Center in Bedminster, NJ to Asana Partners
Fully leased, anchored by Kings Food Markets and CVS; Kings Food Markets and CVS anchor with Starbucks, banks, dining
Buyer signals confidence in Somerset County retail strength; demographics and limited competition cited
stories.summary: JLL Capital Markets closed the sale of The Hills Village Center, a 110,000-square-foot fully leased grocery-anchored retail property in Bedminster, New Jersey, to Asana Partners. The asset is anchored by Kings Food Markets and CVS and features strong secondary tenants including Starbucks, PNC Bank, Peapack Gladstone Bank, and multiple dining and service retailers. JLL's marketing language emphasized strong demographics and limited retail competition in Somerset County as drivers of investor interest.
stories.impact: Investor appetite for grocery-anchored retail in Somerset County (Central/Northern NJ) reflects stable neighborhood demographics and resilient local spending. This signals residential stability and household formation in the North Jersey suburbs, supporting baseline demand for multifamily product in proximate markets. Limited retail supply competition also suggests underserved population growth, a leading indicator for residential development feasibility in this suburban corridor.

stories.title: Davis Names Managing Director for Mixed-Use Development
stories.excerpt: The Davis Companies has appointed Melissa Schrock to the newly created position of managing director of mixed-use Development. Schrock will oversee Davis’ growing portfolio of mixed-use properties nationwide, supporting all project aspects including acquisition, entitlement and ground-up development. “Davis has deep experience navigating complex development opportunities and working collaboratively with tenants, partners, stakeholders and communities,” said Schrock. “I look forward to building on that experience and helping advance projects that contribute to the long-term vitality of the places in which we work.” Before joining Davis, Schrock served as EVP of mixed-use development at HRP Group, where she led the firm’s expansion into the urban mixed-use space, supporting five million square feet of mixed-use and life science innovation projects across the country. These included 776 Summer in Boston, a 19-acre site on the Potomac River in Alexandria, VA and the Innovation Campus at the Bellwether District in Philadelphia. She previously worked as VP of development at BXP and as development manager at Samuels & Associates. The post Davis Names Managing Director for Mixed-Use Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Davis Companies appointed Melissa Schrock as managing director of mixed-use development
Schrock led $5M-sf mixed-use and life science projects at HRP Group across Boston, Alexandria, Philadelphia
Davis expanding mixed-use portfolio nationwide across acquisition, entitlement, and ground-up development
stories.summary: The Davis Companies created a new managing director position for mixed-use development and appointed Melissa Schrock, who previously led mixed-use and life science expansion at HRP Group. Schrock managed over 5 million square feet of projects including 776 Summer in Boston, a 19-acre Potomac River site in Alexandria, and the Innovation Campus at Bellwether District in Philadelphia. Her mandate is to oversee Davis' growing mixed-use portfolio nationwide across acquisition, entitlement, and ground-up development.
stories.impact: Davis' institutional pivot toward mixed-use development—hiring a dedicated managing director—signals a larger developer's strategic shift to integrated residential-plus-retail-plus-office projects in urban and innovation-focused submarkets. This suggests multifamily operators are increasingly bundling residential with experiential, office, and F&B components to command higher rents and occupancy. Developers should expect intensified competition for urban infill and mixed-use entitlements, particularly in innovation districts (Boston, Northern VA, Philadelphia), where land scarcity and demand favor projects that maximize use density.

stories.title: Transamerica Pyramid Center Continues 2026 Leasing Momentum
stories.excerpt: JLL and YODA Group have completed more than 13,000 square feet of new leasing activity across Transamerica Pyramid Center in San Francisco. The transactions include a new lease with a leading New York-based multi-stage VC firm, as well as the renewal by a San Francisco-based law firm, which has renewed and expanded its 7,000 square foot occupancy in Two Transamerica. “San Francisco’s office market has entered a new phase, with leasing activity accelerating and companies increasingly making longer-term decisions about their workplace needs,” said Chris Roeder, vice chairman at JLL San Francisco. “The strongest demand continues to gravitate toward high-quality buildings in the most vibrant neighborhoods, specifically those that can offer the location, amenities and overall experience companies need to attract talent. Transamerica Pyramid Center is well positioned to capture that demand as the market continues to strengthen. The latest transactions bring year-to-date leasing activity to nine deals spanning approximately 126,000 square feet. They come as ownership continues to advance new investments throughout the property. The post Transamerica Pyramid Center Continues 2026 Leasing Momentum appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL/YODA Group completed 13k-sf new leasing at Transamerica Pyramid Center, San Francisco
New York-based multi-stage VC firm signed lease; SF law firm renewed/expanded 7k-sf occupancy
YTD 2026: 126k-sf across nine deals; market entering new phase with longer-term tenant commitments
stories.summary: JLL and YODA Group closed more than 13,000 square feet of office leases at San Francisco's Transamerica Pyramid Center, including a new tenant (a New York-based multi-stage VC firm) and a renewal/expansion by a local law firm. Year-to-date 2026 leasing totals 126,000 square feet across nine deals. Market commentary indicates San Francisco's office sector is entering a recovery phase with companies making longer-term workplace commitments and strong demand concentrating in high-amenity buildings in vibrant neighborhoods.
stories.impact: San Francisco office market stabilization and VC firm relocation from NYC to SF signals talent and capital clustering in the Bay Area. This reinforces residential demand for renter-occupied apartments in walkable, amenity-rich neighborhoods (SOMA, Mission, downtown SF). Multifamily developers should prioritize urban infill projects with proximity to premium office and VC hubs, as tech sector job recovery and expanded work-in-office policies will drive apartment demand and rent growth in SF core markets over 2026–2027.

stories.title: Malaysian Bank, Medical Practice Sign Leases at 575 Madison Avenue
stories.excerpt: A Malaysian bank and a concierge medical service together took more than 14,100 square feet of office space in Midtown. Malayan Banking Berhad, also known as Maybank, signed the largest of the two deals with 8,629 square feet across the entire 24th floor of Steinberg & Pokoik Management’s 575 Madison Avenue, according to landlord broker CBRE. CBRE did not disclose the asking rent, but the average asking rent for office space in Midtown in the third quarter of 2026 was $85.08 per square foot, according to a report from Colliers. Maybank will relocate its New York City offices from 400 Park Avenue about three blocks away. Meanwhile, the smaller of the two deals was for Park 55 Medical Associates, where Dr. Wendy Ziecheck and Dr. Christopher Barley will practice medicine. Park 55 leased 5,474 square feet on part of the 10th and 15th floors of the building. “575 Madison Avenue attracts leading financial services and professional services tenants seeking a prestigious address and exceptional building amenities,” CBRE’s Gregg Rothkin said in a statement. “These latest transactions underscore the demand for high-quality office space in a premier Midtown location.” Rothkin negotiated on behalf of the landlord alongside CBRE’s David Hollander, Brad Auerbach, Maxwell Tarter and William Hooks, but it’s unclear who represented the tenants in the deals. In a third deal, another concierge health clinic, which CBRE declined to identify, leased 14,211 square feet at 575 Madison, according to the brokerage. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Maybank (Malaysian bank) leased 8,629 sf on entire 24th floor of 575 Madison Avenue, Midtown
Park 55 Medical Associates leased 5,474 sf; Maybank relocating from 400 Park Ave (3 blocks away)
Midtown Q3 2026 asking rent: $85.08/sf; attracts financial services and professional services tenants
stories.summary: Maybank leased 8,629 square feet across the entire 24th floor of 575 Madison Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, relocating from 400 Park Avenue three blocks away. Park 55 Medical Associates concurrently leased 5,474 square feet across two floors. Midtown's average asking rent in Q3 2026 was $85.08 per square foot. The deals underscore 575 Madison Avenue's appeal to premium financial services and professional services tenants seeking prestigious addresses and building amenities.
stories.impact: Financial services and professional services firms continuing to lease and relocate within Midtown signals stabilization and modest growth in NYC office occupancy. However, the intra-Midtown move (Maybank) rather than cross-metro relocation limits net job inflow to NYC. Multifamily developers should monitor whether office leasing translates to sustained renter demand in adjacent residential neighborhoods (Midtown East, Hell's Kitchen, Upper East Side). Without significant net employment growth, residential demand will remain constrained; focus underwriting on quality assets in walkable submarkets with diverse employment anchors (tech, healthcare, media) rather than office-dependent corridors.

stories.title: Helaba Provides $105M Construction Takeout Loan on Nashville Apartments
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between CrossHarbor Capital Partners and Mill Creek Residential has secured $105 million of construction takeout financing for a newly built mixed-use project in Nashville, Commercial Observer has learned. German commercial bank Helaba supplied the bridge loan for the sponsorship’s Modera Riverview development that debuted in 2024 in Nashville’s Germantown neighborhood. PNC previously provided a $103 million construction loan for the 400-unit property, which also features 13,998 square feet of retail space. Located at 1410 Adams Street, off the west shore of the Cumberland River two miles north of Downtown Nashville, Modera Riverview has resident amenities that include a swimming pool, a rooftop lounge, a fitness center, coworking spaces and a golf simulator. The ground-floor retail space is 100 percent leased to Legacy Fitness and Italian restaurant Indaco. Jason Deck, director of real estate finance at Helaba, said having two “highly experienced multifamily operators” and a property in a city with strong momentum made the deal attractive. “Nashville continues to perform well and remains an important market for our U.S. real estate platform,” Deck said in a statement. CrossHarbor Capital Partners and Mill Creek Residential did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Helaba provided $105M construction takeout financing for Modera Riverview, Nashville (CrossHarbor/Mill Creek JV)
400-unit mixed-use project (13,998 sf retail) in Germantown, Nashville; opened 2024, fully occupied retail
PNC provided $103M construction loan; Bridge financing signals strong exit appetite for Nashville multifamily
stories.summary: CrossHarbor Capital Partners and Mill Creek Residential secured $105 million of construction takeout financing from German bank Helaba for Modera Riverview, a 400-unit mixed-use project in Nashville's Germantown neighborhood that delivered in 2024. The property includes 13,998 square feet of ground-floor retail (100% leased to Legacy Fitness and Indaco restaurant) and amenities including a pool, rooftop lounge, fitness center, coworking, and golf simulator. PNC previously provided the $103 million construction loan.
stories.impact: Active construction takeout financing and full retail occupancy at a 400-unit Nashville multifamily project signals strong lender and tenant demand for quality product in Nashville's growth corridors. Germantown's waterfront location (west of Cumberland River) and lifestyle amenities reflect developer confidence in Nashville's renter demographic (young professionals, remote workers). The quick progression from construction to stabilization and bridge financing indicates strong lease-up and rent trajectory, supporting continued development velocity in Nashville's urban submarkets. Multifamily developers should prioritize Nashville acquisitions and ground-up starts in mixed-use, walkable neighborhoods with retail and F&B appeal.

stories.title: Joyland Sells Staten Island Shopping Center for $57M
stories.excerpt: South Shore Commons, a popular shopping and dining plaza on Staten Island, has sold for the second time in four years. Joyland Management sold the 157,347-square-foot outdoor shopping center at 2965 Veterans Road West for $57 million, or $362 per square foot, to real estate investment trust Phillips Edison & Company, which owns and manages grocery-anchored shopping centers across the U.S. A source with knowledge of the deal confirmed the transaction. Traded first reported the deal. Spokespeople for the buyer and seller did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. Joel Wertzberger, Judy Wolcowitz and Jack Wolcowitz of Joyland Management handled the sale in-house, while Newmark’s Daniel O’Brien, Conor Lalor, Caroline Hodes, Loren Valla, Felton Hatcher and Adam Spies represented the seller and procured the buyer. Newmark did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Jack Wolcowitz bought South Shore Commons in 2022 for an undisclosed amount. Joyland refinanced the property in 2023 for $41.8 million. The property changed hands before that in 2018 for $41 million. The tenant roster at South Shore Commons includes Filoncino Bakery Cafe, Dunkin, Pronto Pizza, Sola Salon Studios, Retro Fitness and Sally Beauty. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Joyland Management sold South Shore Commons, Staten Island (157k-sf) to Phillips Edison for $57M ($362/sf)
Property is grocery-anchored shopping center; second sale in four years; sold to REIT operator
Joyland purchased property in 2022 (price undisclosed); refinanced in 2023 for $41.8M
stories.summary: Joyland Management sold South Shore Commons, a 157,347-square-foot grocery-anchored shopping center on Staten Island, to Phillips Edison & Company (a national REIT) for $57 million, or $362 per square foot. This marks the property's second sale in four years. Joyland had acquired the asset in 2022 at an undisclosed price and refinanced it in 2023 for $41.8 million.
stories.impact: A REIT's acquisition of a grocery-anchored center on Staten Island at $362/sf reflects stable fundamentals in outer-borough NYC retail and underlying residential demographics. The rapid turnover (2022 purchase, 2025 exit) at modest unit economics ($57M for 157k sf) suggests limited value-add opportunity and compressed cap rates, indicating limited distress but also limited upside in secondary retail. For multifamily: stable, REIT-managed retail in outer boroughs supports neighborhood-level consumer services and foot traffic, sustaining rental demand in adjacent residential markets. However, limited new development or capital intensity in retail suggests focused attention on residential redevelopment or conversion opportunities in Staten Island's dense neighborhoods rather than retail-forward mixed-use plays.
